title: Financial Accounting
description: Financial Accounting develops the ability to prepare, connect, interpret, and challenge financial reports. Students move from economic events and controlled transaction records to accrual statements, disclosures, cash-flow analysis, earnings-quality assessment, and an integrated real-company decision. The unified core is common to all seven degrees. Examples, studios, and the capstone supply discipline-specific relevance.

resources.title: Principles of Accounting, Volume 1: Financial Accounting
resources.description: OpenStax. Free common spine for accounting and non-accounting majors, with practice, examples, and review.

resources.title: Financial Accounting (Libby, Libby, and Hodge)
resources.description: Decision-oriented introduction with strong statement linkage and real-company context.

resources.title: Financial Accounting: Tools for Business Decision Making
resources.description: Kimmel, Weygandt, and Kieso. Accessible mechanics-to-decisions pathway with broad cross-major usability.

resources.title: Financial Accounting (Spiceland, Thomas, and Herrmann)
resources.description: Clear conceptual development and a strong bridge toward intermediate reporting.

resources.title: Hospitality Financial Accounting
resources.description: Weygandt, Kimmel, and Kieso. Industry cases for property, food and beverage, receivables, controls, and operating interpretation.

resources.title: Financial Statement Analysis and Security Valuation
resources.description: Stephen Penman. Selective enrichment for earnings quality, forecasting, profitability, and valuation links.

resources.title: Financial Statement Analysis and Valuation
resources.description: Easton, McAnally, Sommers, and Zhang. Integrated real-company analysis, forecasting, and valuation bridge.

resources.title: Financial Shenanigans
resources.description: Schilit, Perler, and Engelhart. Case-based identification of earnings, cash-flow, and key-metric manipulation risks.

resources.title: SEC EDGAR Search Filings
resources.description: Primary source for 10-Ks, 10-Qs, filing HTML, full-text search, Inline XBRL, and filing APIs.

resources.title: FASB Conceptual Framework
resources.description: Objectives, elements, recognition, measurement, presentation, and disclosure concepts.

resources.title: FASB Accounting Standards Codification
resources.description: Authoritative U.S. GAAP research orientation. Access terms vary.

resources.title: IFRS Accounting Standards and supporting materials
resources.description: Authoritative IFRS context, conceptual framework, and implementation support.

resources.title: MIT Sloan 15.515 Financial Accounting
resources.description: Lecture notes, problems, annual-report work, and graduate-level case framing.

resources.title: AccountingCoach
resources.description: Short explanations and drills for mechanics. Verify technical conclusions against authoritative guidance.

resources.title: Farhat Lectures
resources.description: Long-form worked instruction across financial accounting, reporting, audit, and exam preparation.

resources.title: Edspira
resources.description: Concise worked explanations for entries, statements, ratios, and reporting topics.

resources.title: Accounting Stuff
resources.description: Beginner-friendly visual explanations useful for pre-class preparation and review.

topics.title: Financial Reporting Purpose, Ethics, Users, Standards, and Information Ecosystem
topics.description: The course begins with why financial reporting exists: to communicate decision-useful information about resources, claims, performance, and cash flows while operating within standards, governance, controls, audits, and ethical duties.

children.title: Decision usefulness and stewardship
children.description: Financial reports help capital providers and other stakeholders allocate resources and assess how management used entrusted resources.

children.title: Employee, supplier, regulator, and community perspectives
Financial position, performance, and cash-flow questions
Conceptual framework
children.description: A conceptual framework organizes the objectives, qualitative characteristics, elements, recognition, measurement, presentation, and disclosure choices behind reporting.

children.title: Assets, liabilities, equity, income, expenses, gains, and losses
Standard setting and reporting jurisdictions
children.description: Students learn where authoritative guidance comes from and why similar transactions may be reported differently across jurisdictions.

children.title: Governance, assurance, and ethics
children.description: Reliable reporting depends on ethical judgment, governance, controls, and independent assurance as well as technical rules.

children.title: Independent auditor role and reasonable assurance
Annual report and filing ecosystem
children.description: A filing combines audited statements with management narrative, risks, governance information, and detailed notes that must be read together.

topics.title: Accounting Equation, Business Models, and Linked Financial Statements
topics.description: Students translate economic events and a firm's business model into the linked statements, then read the statements as one coherent representation rather than four isolated schedules.

children.title: Accounting equation
children.description: Students learn the core relationship that keeps accounting records in balance. The gist is that every transaction affects assets, liabilities, equity, or some combination of them.

children.title: Expanded equation with revenues, expenses, and dividends
Four primary financial statements
children.description: Students learn what each statement is designed to communicate. The point is to see statements as connected views of the same business.

children.title: Statement of retained earnings or shareholders' equity
Users and decision usefulness
children.description: Financial accounting exists because users need credible information. Students learn how different users read the same reports for different decisions.

children.title: Reporting assumptions and qualities
children.description: Students learn the basic assumptions that make accounting information comparable and useful.

children.title: Relevance, faithful representation, comparability, and consistency
Business model to financial architecture
children.description: The operating model explains why particular assets, obligations, revenues, expenses, and cash-flow patterns appear.

children.title: Service, merchandising, manufacturing, hospitality, and platform examples

topics.title: Transaction Analysis, Debits and Credits, Journals, Ledgers, and Data Trails
topics.description: Students build precise transaction fluency and connect each entry to evidence, controls, system records, and downstream financial-statement effects.

children.title: Transaction analysis
children.description: Students learn to identify what changed in the business and why. The gist is to translate business events into accounting effects.

children.title: Debits and credits
children.description: Debits and credits are a recording system, not a moral judgment about good and bad. Students learn which accounts increase or decrease on each side.

children.title: Journals and ledgers
children.description: Students learn the flow from chronological records to account-by-account balances. This is the backbone of the accounting information system.

children.title: Trial balance
children.description: A trial balance checks whether total debits equal total credits. Students learn what it can and cannot catch.

children.title: Errors not revealed by a trial balance
Accounting information systems and audit trails
children.description: Modern systems automate posting, but users still need to understand how source data becomes a controlled, reviewable record.

children.title: Error tracing from statement to source

topics.title: Accounting Cycle, Accruals, Adjustments, Estimates, Closing, and Error Correction
topics.description: Students complete a reporting period from raw transactions through adjusted statements, while learning why estimates, controls, and review matter at the close.

children.title: Accounting cycle overview
children.description: Students learn the recurring steps used to record, adjust, report, and reset accounts each period.

children.title: Adjusting entries
children.description: Adjustments make records match accrual accounting. The point is to report revenues and expenses in the correct period.

children.title: Adjusted trial balance and statements
children.description: Students learn how adjusted balances feed the statements. This connects bookkeeping mechanics to external reporting.

children.title: Closing process
children.description: Closing resets temporary accounts for the next period. Students learn why revenue, expense, and dividend accounts do not carry forward like balance sheet accounts.

children.title: Estimates, errors, and close quality
children.description: Closing the books requires judgment and disciplined review, not only mechanical completion.

children.title: Close checklist, review evidence, and post-close analytics

topics.title: Revenue Recognition, Expenses, Contracts, and Earnings Measurement
topics.description: Students decide when performance creates revenue and when resource consumption becomes expense, then examine how contract terms and estimates shape reported earnings.

children.title: Accrual versus cash basis
children.description: Students learn why financial reporting uses accrual accounting. The gist is that performance should be reported when earned or incurred, not only when cash changes hands.

children.title: Revenue recognition
children.description: Revenue recognition determines when a company can report sales. Students learn the basic logic behind modern revenue rules without needing full ASC 606 technical depth.

children.title: Expense recognition and matching
children.description: Students learn to connect expenses to the revenues or periods they help generate. This supports more meaningful income measurement.

children.title: Earnings management risk
children.description: Timing judgments create room for aggressive reporting. Students learn why revenue and expense recognition are common places for red flags.

children.title: Contract analysis and the ASC 606 / IFRS 15 model
children.description: A structured contract model turns commercial promises, prices, and fulfillment into timing and measurement decisions.

children.title: Recognize revenue as obligations are satisfied
Contract assets, contract liabilities, and disclosures

topics.title: Cash, Receivables, Credit Losses, Internal Control, and Fraud Risk
topics.description: Students protect and measure liquid resources, estimate collectible amounts, and understand how control design reduces error, theft, and misstatement risk.

children.title: Cash and bank reconciliation
children.description: Students learn why book cash and bank cash often differ. The gist is to reconcile timing differences and errors before relying on cash balances.

children.title: Internal controls
children.description: Controls reduce errors, fraud, and misuse of assets. Students learn practical safeguards that support reliable reporting.

children.title: Accounts receivable
children.description: Students learn how credit sales create receivables and collection risk. This connects sales growth to working capital quality.

children.title: Bad debt accounting
children.description: Bad debt estimates make receivables more realistic. Students learn why uncollectible accounts are estimated before specific customers default.

children.title: Fraud risk and control evaluation
children.description: Controls are evaluated by the risks they address, the evidence they create, and the ways management override or collusion can defeat them.

children.title: Cash, payroll, purchasing, and revenue-cycle risks

topics.title: Inventory, Cost of Goods Sold, Valuation, and Supply-Chain Economics
topics.description: Students connect physical flows, cost assignments, write-downs, margins, and working-capital consequences across retail, hospitality, manufacturing, and supply networks.

children.title: Inventory systems
children.description: Students learn how companies track inventory and cost of goods sold. The point is to understand timing and recordkeeping choices.

children.title: Cost flow assumptions
children.description: Cost flow assumptions determine which costs go to inventory and which go to expense. Students learn that these are accounting assumptions, not always physical flow.

children.title: Lower-of-cost-or-market / net realizable value
children.description: Students learn why inventory may need to be written down. The gist is that assets should not be carried above recoverable value.

children.title: Inventory analysis
children.description: Students learn how inventory choices affect analysis of profitability and efficiency.

children.title: Effects of inflation on FIFO and LIFO
Inventory controls and supply-chain interpretation
children.description: Inventory accounting becomes decision-useful when records, physical custody, loss, obsolescence, and cash conversion are analyzed together.

children.title: Days inventory outstanding and cash conversion
Restaurant, hotel, retail, and manufacturing patterns

topics.title: Long-Lived Assets, Intangibles, Depreciation, Impairment, and R&D
topics.description: Students distinguish investment from period cost and evaluate how useful lives, residual values, impairment, and internally generated intangibles affect performance.

children.title: Property, plant, and equipment
children.description: Students learn what costs are capitalized when an asset is acquired and prepared for use.

children.title: Depreciation methods
children.description: Depreciation allocates asset cost over useful life. Students learn how method choice affects income and book value.

children.title: Residual value and useful life estimates
Intangible assets and amortization
children.description: Students learn how nonphysical assets are reported. The gist is to distinguish finite-life assets from assets with indefinite lives.

children.title: Impairment
children.description: Impairment recognizes when an asset's carrying value is no longer recoverable. Students learn how this protects statement users from overstated assets.

children.title: Research, development, software, and estimation
children.description: Knowledge investment exposes the limits of balance sheets and the importance of policy and estimation choices.

children.title: Changes in useful life and residual value

topics.title: Liabilities, Contingencies, Bonds, Leases, and Time Value
topics.description: Students measure present obligations, connect financing terms to interest and cash flows, and look beyond headline debt to contractual and contingent claims.

children.title: Current liabilities
children.description: Students learn which obligations are due soon and why they matter for liquidity. The gist is to connect short-term obligations to cash planning.

children.title: Long-term debt and bonds
children.description: Students learn how companies borrow for longer periods and report interest costs. This supports analysis of leverage and solvency.

children.title: Leases
children.description: Leases can create both asset use rights and liabilities. Students learn why lease reporting matters for off-balance-sheet risk.

children.title: Contingencies and commitments
children.description: Some obligations depend on uncertain future events. Students learn how recognition and disclosure depend on probability and estimability.

children.title: Time value and debt analytics
children.description: Present-value reasoning explains why contractual cash flows and stated amounts can produce different carrying values and economic risks.

topics.title: Income Taxes, Deferred Taxes, Pensions, and Other Long-Term Obligations
topics.description: This selective bridge module helps students recognize major obligations whose economics unfold over time. The goal is interpretation and statement linkage, not full intermediate-accounting computation.

children.title: Book income, taxable income, and current tax
children.description: Financial reporting and tax systems pursue different purposes, so pretax accounting income rarely equals taxable income.

children.title: Deferred tax assets and liabilities
children.description: Temporary differences shift tax effects across periods and create balance-sheet amounts that reverse as assets are recovered or liabilities are settled.

children.title: Pensions and postretirement obligations
children.description: Long-duration employee promises combine service cost, funding, actuarial assumptions, and disclosure complexity.

children.title: Other long-term and off-balance-sheet exposures
children.description: Commitments and guarantees can matter economically even when recognition is limited or delayed.

topics.title: Equity, Dividends, Share-Based Compensation, Treasury Stock, and EPS
topics.description: Students trace claims of owners, distributions, repurchases, compensation, and per-share performance while distinguishing accounting equity from market value.

children.title: Contributed capital
children.description: Students learn how corporations record investments from shareholders. The gist is to separate legal capital from additional paid-in capital.

children.title: Retained earnings and dividends
children.description: Retained earnings show accumulated profits kept in the business. Students learn how dividends distribute value to owners.

children.title: Treasury stock
children.description: Treasury stock records shares repurchased by the company. Students learn how buybacks affect equity and per-share metrics.

children.title: Earnings per share
children.description: EPS is a widely used performance measure. Students learn its basic calculation and why analysts care about dilution.

children.title: Share-based compensation and ownership analysis
children.description: Equity awards align incentives but create expense, dilution, valuation, and disclosure questions.

children.title: Options, restricted shares, and performance awards
Book value, market capitalization, and ownership structure

topics.title: Investments, Fair Value, Influence, and Consolidated Reporting Preview
topics.description: This selective bridge module explains how ownership and influence determine reporting. Students learn to interpret investment balances and group statements without attempting a full advanced-consolidation course.

children.title: Debt and equity investments
children.description: The business purpose and reporting classification of an investment shape where value changes and income appear.

children.title: Fair-value measurement
children.description: Fair value estimates become less observable as markets thin, increasing the importance of valuation methods, controls, and disclosure.

children.title: Influence, control, and reporting method
children.description: Ownership percentage is evidence, not the whole answer. The degree of influence or control determines the reporting model.

children.title: Acquisitions, goodwill, and related parties
children.description: Group reporting asks what was acquired, how consideration was measured, and whether transactions occurred at arm's length.

topics.title: Statement of Cash Flows, Working Capital, and Cash Conversion
topics.description: Students reconcile accrual performance to cash generation, diagnose working-capital movements, and distinguish sustainable operating cash from financing or timing effects.

children.title: Cash flow statement structure
children.description: Students learn the three categories of cash flow. The point is to separate operations, investment, and financing decisions.

children.title: Operating cash flow
children.description: Students learn how operations generate or consume cash. This helps them compare cash performance with accrual earnings.

children.title: Investing and financing cash flows
children.description: Students learn how asset investment and financing choices appear in cash flow reporting.

children.title: Purchases and sales of long-lived assets
Noncash transactions
children.description: Important financing and investing events may not use cash immediately. Students learn why disclosure still matters.

children.title: Working capital and cash-conversion diagnosis
children.description: Receivables, inventory, and payables reveal how operations consume or release cash and where business-model comparisons can mislead.

topics.title: Financial Statement Analysis, DuPont, Segments, and Peer Benchmarking
topics.description: Students turn statements and notes into a structured view of profitability, liquidity, solvency, efficiency, risk, and the economic drivers behind differences.

children.title: Analysis framework
children.description: Students learn to move from numbers to questions. The gist is that ratios are tools for diagnosis, not answers by themselves.

children.title: Liquidity and solvency ratios
children.description: Students learn how to assess short-term and long-term financial risk.

children.title: Profitability and efficiency ratios
children.description: Students learn how to evaluate margins, asset use, and returns.

children.title: Peer benchmarking
children.description: Benchmarking gives ratios meaning. Students learn to compare companies carefully while accounting for business models and accounting choices.

children.title: DuPont, segment, and degree-lens analysis
children.description: Decomposition separates margins, asset use, and leverage while segment and operating context keep ratios from becoming mechanical scorecards.

children.title: Hospitality occupancy, ADR, and RevPAR links
HR payroll, benefits, and human-capital disclosure links
Supply-chain working capital and asset utilization
Finance valuation inputs and MBA capital-allocation questions

topics.title: Disclosure, Accounting Choices, Earnings Quality, Non-GAAP Measures, and Forensics
topics.description: Students learn that reported numbers are inseparable from policy choices, estimates, controls, governance, audits, disclosures, and management communication.

children.title: GAAP, IFRS, and standard setting
children.description: Students learn who makes reporting rules and why standards matter. The point is to understand accounting as an institutional system, not just bookkeeping.

children.title: Disclosures and footnotes
children.description: Footnotes often contain the details needed to interpret the statements. Students learn to read disclosures as part of the report, not extra decoration.

children.title: Earnings quality and red flags
children.description: Students learn to distinguish reported earnings from sustainable performance. This is where accounting choices meet analysis.

children.title: SEC filings and integrated company analysis
children.description: Students practice reading real filings. The final goal is to connect statements, footnotes, ratios, risks, and business context into one coherent view.

children.title: Digital reporting, comparability, and emerging disclosure
children.description: Modern analysis increasingly combines narrative disclosure, tagged data, and cross-standard comparison while respecting materiality and assurance limits.

children.title: Data provenance and AI-assisted analysis controls

topics.title: Real-Company Filing Lab, Forecasting, Integrated Analysis, and Decision Memo
topics.description: The capstone requires students to use a real filing, reconcile the statements and notes, test accounting quality, build a compact forecast, and communicate a decision tailored to their degree context.

children.title: Filing navigation and data provenance
children.description: Students learn to locate authoritative figures, trace them to statements and notes, and preserve an auditable path from source to conclusion.

children.title: Normalization and earnings quality
children.description: A useful baseline distinguishes recurring operating performance from accounting choices, transitory items, and financing effects.

children.title: Integrated forecast
children.description: A compact forecast forces assumptions about revenue, margins, working capital, investment, financing, and taxes to reconcile across the statements.

children.title: Decision memo and defense
children.description: Students communicate what the evidence supports, what remains uncertain, and what decision should follow.

children.title: Degree-context application
children.description: Every student meets the same accounting standard while applying it to the decisions most relevant to the participating programs.

children.title: Business Administration: strategy, operating drivers, and capital allocation
Accounting: entries, standards research, controls, and close quality
Finance: earnings quality, leverage, cash flow, and valuation inputs
Hospitality Management: property intensity, seasonality, inventory, and RevPAR-related interpretation
Human Resources: payroll, benefits, pensions, share-based pay, and workforce disclosures
Supply Chain Management: inventory, supplier terms, working capital, asset utilization, and disruptions
MBA: integrated performance, risk, governance, and executive recommendation
